extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidance for creating, structuring, performing, and editing stand-up comedy material with emphasis on persona, architecture of the set, withheld-punchline technique, and live editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withheld-Punchline Doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: REMOVE THE PUNCHLINE. Build tension, never release. The audience laughs out of accumulated unresolved expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audience eventually laughs at the WAITING itself. This destabilizes the contract: laughter becomes complicit, self-conscious. Use unresolved expectation as the engine of response rather than a traditional release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy as Architecture / Set Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bit is a building block toward an evening's structure; the set is composed and the audience experiences it as inevitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence matters as much as material. Think of bits as parts of a larger engineered structure rather than isolated jokes; design flow and inevitability across the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persona as Performance Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a persona (e.g., Martin's 'wild and crazy') as a costume for sincerity so absurdity reads as character rather than a mere joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The persona must allow you to perform absurdity with full commitment. Without a credible persona, absurdity will read as a punchline instead of character truth. Choose and sustain a persona that 'earns' the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and Ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be so good they can't ignore you." Don't borrow other comics' rhythms — they read as imitation. Find one structural choice that nobody else makes; own it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek a distinct structural or formal choice that differentiates your work. Avoid copying rhythms or approaches of others; claim a single defining feature and develop it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowing When to Walk Away / Reinvention
rubrics_metrics.description: Walk away from a form at its peak if it has nothing more to give you; reinvent rather than repeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding when the form no longer serves you is part of craft — choose reinvention over repetition to preserve integrity and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing for the Live Show
rubrics_metrics.description: Material is rewritten on stage, not at the desk. Audience reaction is the only data that matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cuts come fast; additions come slow. Use live performance as the editing laboratory: trim aggressively based on what survives the audience and be conservative about adding new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the audience getting what they expect, or learning to want something new?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a bit satisfies existing expectations or trains the audience to seek novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to shift audience desire toward new patterns; use expectation strategically (including withholding resolution) to teach the audience what to want next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the bit a piece of architecture, not a free-standing joke?
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask whether the bit functions as an element of a larger compositional structure rather than an isolated punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer material that contributes to the set's overall arc and inevitability. Avoid bits that feel disposable or detached from the evening's architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does your persona earn the absurdity?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess if the chosen persona makes the absurd material believable and emotionally coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A persona should justify the absurdity through commitment and consistency; if it doesn't, the absurdity will read as mere joke-work and fall flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there one structural choice that's distinctly yours?
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm you have one clear, owned formal or structural decision that differentiates your work from others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could be withholding punchlines, a delivery rhythm, a recurring motif, or any singular formal stance — cultivate and protect it as your signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you cut everything that didn't survive the audience?
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure material that fails in front of audiences is removed rather than preserved out of attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience feedback as the decisive criterion for cuts; be ruthless in removing material that doesn't earn laughs or advance the set's architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you adding to the form, or repeating it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether your work innovates within the comedic form or merely repeats existing conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to add formally or structurally to the art of stand-up (e.g., new uses of expectation, persona, sequence) rather than rehashing familiar patterns.
